lessons.title: The Power of Compound Growth
objectives: Compute compound growth with A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt).
Estimate doubling time with the Rule of 72.
lessons.hook: A penny doubled daily for 30 days vs. $1 million today. Which would you choose?

notes.body: Each period multiplies the balance by (1 + r/n).
72 ÷ rate ≈ years to double; good for quick estimates.

discussion: Where else do you see exponential growth?
misconceptions: Doubling the rate doubles the result.
reflection: How would you explain compound growth to a friend?
lessons.extension: Graph balances for 3%, 6%, and 9% on the same axes.

extend: Derive the Rule of 72 from logarithms.

lessons.realWorld: Investment returns are not fixed; projections use assumptions.

lessons.title: Recurring Contributions and the Cost of Waiting
objectives: Compute the future value of regular deposits.
Find the deposit needed to reach a goal.
lessons.hook: Use the Decision Lab “The Cost of Waiting” — predict which of three friends wins.

notes.body: FV = PMT((1 + i)^N − 1) ÷ i for end-of-period deposits.
Automatic contributions build consistency and use dollar-cost averaging.

discussion: What could keep someone from starting early?
misconceptions: I can catch up later easily.
Compute the payment needed to catch up after a 10-year delay.
reflection: What is a realistic first monthly contribution for you?

extend: Model contributions that increase 3% per year.

lessons.realWorld: Many employers offer automatic payroll contributions to retirement plans.

lessons.title: Comparing Investment Scenarios
objectives: Compare projected outcomes under different return assumptions.
Quantify the long-term impact of fees.
lessons.hook: Two funds hold the exact same stocks. Why might one leave you $20,000 poorer?

notes.body: Savings (stable, low), bonds (moderate), stocks (higher expected return, more volatility).
Net return = gross return − expense ratio.

discussion: Why might someone choose lower expected returns?
reflection: What would you look for in a first investment fund?
lessons.extension: Compare expense ratios of three real index funds (public data).

extend: Include inflation and compute real ending values.

lessons.realWorld: Fund fact sheets list expense ratios and historical returns with disclaimers.

lessons.title: Understanding Investment Risk
objectives: Describe volatility and its effect on returns.
Match investments to goals and risk tolerance.
lessons.hook: Flip coins to simulate “market years” (+20% heads, −10% tails) for 10 years. Compare class results.

notes.body: Losses need larger gains to recover; uneven returns end below the simple average.
Many holdings reduce the impact of any single failure.
Short-term money should not depend on volatile assets.

discussion: How would you feel if your investment dropped 25%? What would you do?
lessons.extension: Research a historical market downturn and the recovery time.

extend: Simulate 1,000 random 10-year paths in a spreadsheet.

lessons.realWorld: Investment disclosures always state that past performance does not guarantee future results.
